title: Tensor extension, local free presentations and Hom comparison
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its Zariski site [def-sc-zariski-site] and small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and put $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}(v:V\to T)=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$. Write $L_T=\epsilon_T^*$ for tensor pullback and $R_T=\epsilon_{T,*}$ for restriction to open subschemes along the canonical morphism of ringed sites $\epsilon_T:T_{\mathrm{et}}\to T_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections]. Modules mean sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; Zariski quasi-coherence is [pqf-def-coherent] and site quasi-coherence is [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Then $L_T\dashv R_T$, $L_T$ preserves all small colimits, and $L_T\mathcal O_T\simeq\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$. For each quasi-coherent $F$, there is a canonical natural identification $L_TF(v)=\Gamma(V,v^*F)$, with scalar action and module maps given by pullback of sections [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module, def-pc-module-pullback]. There is an affine open cover $T=\bigcup W_\alpha$ and presentations $\mathcal O_{W_\alpha}^{(I_\alpha)}\to\mathcal O_{W_\alpha}^{(J_\alpha)}\to F|_{W_\alpha}\to0$, whose images under $L_{W_\alpha}$ are free presentations of $(L_TF)|_{(W_\alpha)_{\mathrm{et}}}$; here all index sets are small. In particular $L_TF$ is site quasi-coherent. For each etale $u:V\to T$ there is a natural identification $(L_TF)|_{V_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq L_V(u^*F)$, compatible with module maps and composition. For every open $W\subseteq T$, the adjunction unit $F(W)\to(R_TL_TF)(W)$ is the identity under the displayed section identification. For quasi-coherent $F,H$ the induced map $\operatorname{Hom}(F,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(L_TF,L_TH)$ is bijective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] to the ringed morphism $\epsilon_T$ of [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections]. Its module direct image is precisely $R_T$, with the stated scalar action, so $L_T\dashv R_T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits], $L_T$ preserves every small colimit. These conclusions hold for all modules, not just quasi-coherent ones.

For quasi-coherent $F$, [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-descent] says that $P_F(v)=\Gamma(V,v^*F)$ is already a sheaf. Hence the sheafification in [lem-trf-zariski-etale-tensor-sections] can be removed, using the universal property [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. The comparison is natural in module maps; its scalar action and restrictions are exactly pullback of sections, as specified in the tensor-section comparison. Thus $L_TF=P_F$ canonically as module sheaves.

For etale $u:V\to T$, identify the slice $T_{\mathrm{et}}/V$ with $V_{\mathrm{et}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-site-localization-open]. The restricted ring is literally $\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$ on $a:A\to V$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], $u^*F$ is quasi-coherent, so step 2 applies on $V$. At $a$ the comparison is $\Gamma(A,c_{a,u,F}):\Gamma(A,a^*u^*F)\to\Gamma(A,(u a)^*F)$. The normalized composition and restriction laws [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] make these module isomorphisms a sheaf isomorphism. Their compatibility with module maps is [lem-sc-etale-tensor-sections-map-naturality]. For three successive maps the two composites agree: each is the unique composition comparison normalized by the composite adjunction unit, so uniqueness gives the cocycle equality. This proves the asserted compatibility with composition, as well as restriction to any open subscheme.

source.place: Tag 03FH (remark-change-topologies-ringed-sites (2)); the section formula gives the localized comparison

proof.text: For the unit module, scheme pullback gives $v^*\mathcal O_T\simeq\mathcal O_V$: locally the multiplication map $b\otimes r\mapsto b v^\sharp(r)$ has inverse $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, and the balancing relation proves both composites are identities. These maps respect further pullback and glue. The module $\mathcal O_T$ is quasi-coherent: on each affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ the rank-one case of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] gives $\mathcal O_W\simeq\widetilde A$. Therefore step 2, applied to $\mathcal O_T$, identifies $L_T\mathcal O_T$ with $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$ on every object and restriction. The same applies with any scheme in place of $T$.

Choose an affine open cover $W=\operatorname{Spec}A$ on which $F|_W\simeq\widetilde M$, as permitted by [pqf-def-coherent]. For each such $M$, let $J$ be its underlying set and map $A^{(J)}\to M$ by $e_m\mapsto m$. This is surjective. Let $I$ be the underlying set of its kernel and map $A^{(I)}\to A^{(J)}$ by $e_k\mapsto k$. This exhibits $M$ as the cokernel. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], which preserves all small colimits, to this cokernel and to the coproducts $A^{(I)}$, $A^{(J)}$. The rank-one case of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module] identifies $\widetilde A$ with $\mathcal O_W$, so the resulting presentation is $\mathcal O_W^{(I)}\to\mathcal O_W^{(J)}\to F|_W\to0$. The underlying sets of $M$ and its kernel are small in the module universe; no finite generation is used.

proof.text: Apply $L_W$ to the presentations of step 5. Step 1 preserves the two coproducts and their cokernel; step 4 identifies the unit summands. Step 3 identifies $L_W(F|_W)$ with $(L_TF)|_{W_{\mathrm{et}}}$, using [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction] to replace $F|_W$ by $i_W^*F$. These are the requested free presentations. To check site quasi-coherence on an arbitrary $v:V\to T$, apply step 5 instead to the quasi-coherent module $v^*F$ on $V$ and then apply $L$ on its affine open cover. Step 3 identifies the resulting presentations with restrictions of $L_TF$ to that cover of $V$. Thus the local presentation condition in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] holds for every site object; it is not merely a presentation near the final object.

Here is also the normalization of the unit, which is needed for the Hom claim. For any $M$, restrict a map $P_M^\#\to G$ to $P_M$, then on opens precompose with $\Gamma(W,\kappa_W):M(W)\to\Gamma(W,i_W^*M)$. These components form an $\mathcal O_T$-linear map $M\to R_TG$: for opens $W'\subseteq W$ and $m\in M(W)$, the unit normalization of the composition comparison [lem-sc-etale-qcoherent-presheaf-functorial] sends the restriction of $\eta^{i_W}(m)$ to $\eta^{i_{W'}}(m)$, and the unit equation of $\kappa$ identifies both with $\kappa_{W'}(m|_{W'})$. The sheafification universal property and [lem-trf-etale-tensor-sections-adjunction-extension] give surjectivity of this Hom map, and [lem-trf-etale-tensor-sections-open-determination] gives injectivity. Consequently this is the adjunction Hom bijection for the canonical tensor-section comparison. In particular the identity of $L_TF=P_F$ corresponds to the maps $\Gamma(W,\kappa_W)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-module-pullback-restriction], $\kappa_W$ is the unit-compatible identification of restriction with open pullback. Hence the adjunction unit $F(W)\to P_F(i_W)$ becomes the identity of $F(W)$ under the displayed section identification, for every open $W$, including the empty open.

proof.text: For quasi-coherent $F,H$, adjunction gives $\operatorname{Hom}(L_TF,L_TH)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F,R_TL_TH)$. Step 7 identifies the unit $\eta_H:H\to R_TL_TH$ with an isomorphism (indeed the identity on every open). Thus postcomposition with $\eta_H$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(F,H)\to\operatorname{Hom}(F,R_TL_TH)$. The adjoint of $L_T(h)$ is $R_TL_T(h)\eta_F=\eta_H h$ by naturality of the unit. Therefore the composite bijection is exactly the map $h\mapsto L_T(h)$ in the statement. This proves its bijectivity without assuming any counit is an isomorphism.
